text:
**Short answer: a ~1,000 Wh power station is the sweet spot for one night. My pick is the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh), or the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (also 1,024 Wh) if you want the best fit for this exact job.**

**Why 1,000 Wh works**
- Heated blankets draw little power. The [Tested Watts guide](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) cites about 60 W for a single and 100 W for a double, and Sunbeam rates its full-size blankets at 110 W. At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs one for about 8 hours.
- [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) says a queen blanket is rated about 150 W but cycles to an average of about 75 W. On that basis, 1,000 Wh lasts 11 to 12 hours.
- The sources don't agree on the draw. [HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes about 260 W for a queen. That would need roughly 2,600 Wh for 8 hours, so it is the most conservative estimate. If you run the blanket on high all night, plan for the higher draw. Most people use a lower setting or an auto-off timer, so 1,000 Wh is a reasonable target.

**Specific picks**
1. **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh).** [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) names it the top pick. It says the unit runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, weighs 25 lb, and usually sells for about $380–$500.
2. **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh).** [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists a bundle with a 45W solar panel at $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. The battery is LFP rated for 3,000 cycles, output is 1,800W, and it has a five-year warranty. It's also quiet and fume-free, so you can use it indoors. TechRadar hasn't tested this model itself. It also says the 45W panel is too small to recharge the battery quickly.
3. **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2.** Choose this if you want two nights. [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) says it runs the same blanket for about 23 hours.

**Budget option: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, $289.99).** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) recommends it for one 12 V blanket on low from the car port. It is not enough for a standard 120 V blanket. Blackout Wise says a 286–288 Wh unit gives only about 3–3.5 hours with a 150 W blanket.

**Tips**
- Plug the blanket directly into the station. Sunbeam's manuals say not to use extension cords or power strips ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night)).
- Keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket's folds.
- Don't use a space heater instead. A 1,500 W heater would drain a 1 kWh unit in about 35 minutes ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/)).
- If you also run a CPAP, the pair averages about 109 W. A 1,024 Wh unit lasts about 8 hours in that case ([Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket)).

If you tell me your blanket size and whether you run it on high, I can narrow this down.
